 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. The petitioner has challenged the order at Annexure-A passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, whereby the Special Land Acquisition Officer has directed payment of compensation to the respondent No.3 as regards extent of 4 acres in Sy.No.7/P35 in terms of the package compensation as accepted in terms of Section 29(2) of KIAD Act, 1966.

2. It is noticed from the impugned order that the Special Land Acquisition Officer has taken note that the NC: 2023:KHC:21267 khathedar of the land in Sy.No.7 Muniyamma W/o Kempaiah and her children have executed the sale deed on 09.06.2006 in favour of the father of the claimant D.
Narasimhalu Naidu @ E.N. Naidu.
3. It is noticed that encumbrance was also produced.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer noticed that the father of the claimant died on 22.12.2012.

sentences.text: 4. The Special Land Acquisition Officer has taken note of other impediments for disbursing of compensation and noticed that O.S.No.450/2009 was dismissed for non prosecution.
It is also noticed that O.S.No.404/2020 relates to the persons other than those interested in the present land.
Finding is made that PTCL Act does not apply.
Taking note of the sale deed executed by Muniyamma and her children, direction was made for disbursal of compensation amount in terms of Section 29(2) of KIAD Act.
5. It is noticed that as on date there are no orders of restrain or any other civil suits pending as regards the subject matter of land in Sy.No.7/P35, measuring 4 acres.
There is no material to indicate that the proceedings are initiated under the PTCL Act.

In the absence of which, there are no grounds made NC: 2023:KHC:21267 out to interfere with the order of the Special Land Acquisition Officer for disbursal of compensation on the basis of the sale deed dated 09.06.2006 executed by Muniyamma W/o Kempaiah and her children in favour of the claimants father D.
Narasimhalunaidu @ E.N. Naidu.
6. If the petitioner is aggrieved, he ought to have initiated appropriate proceedings in accordance with law and without challenging the sale deed, no objection of the petitioner can be entertained.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that liberty may be reserved to take out appropriate proceedings in accordance with law.
Needless to state if law permits petitioner is entitled to take out appropriate proceedings.
Accordingly, petition is rejected.

Notice to respondent No.4 is waived of as the contesting party is before this Court.
I.A.No.1/2023 is disposed off as not calling for adjudication in the light of disposal of the main matter itself.
